verdict.rationale: RevenueCat ships official native SDKs, shown in its first-party purchases-ios GitHub repo, plus a documented Web SDK. The docs describe concrete SDK methods such as `purchase(package:)` and `getCustomerInfo()`, and the purchase method works across Apple, Google, and Amazon stores. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of building with the SDKs, and an explicit list of all supported platform SDKs beyond iOS and web.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: Fetch products, make purchases, and check subscription status with our native SDKs.
The SDK has a simple method, `purchase(package:)`, that takes a package from the fetched Offering and purchases the underlying product with Apple, Google, or Amazon.
RevenueCat's Web SDK is an integration path for selling subscriptions and other purchases in your web app.
The latest information can always be retrieved by calling `getCustomerInfo()`
